answer: Agents secure identity by holding unique shards, where a verifier challenges the data inlet to prove continuous custody. Honest participants incur cost to maintain 1,000 active storage shards, while an attacker seeking 1,000 fake identities faces linear growth in storage and retrieval costs, exceeding the profit of collusion. Each shard uses a jade watermark to prevent replay, and a cipher lock ensures only the owner can retrieve proof.
